source.title: Combining Organic and Foliar Fertilization to Enhance Soil Fertility and Mitigate Physiological Disorders of Durian (Durio zibethinus Murr.) Fruit in the Tropics
source.citation: Dang LV, Quyen NK, Ngoc NP, Ly LM, Thao PTP, Hung NN. Plants. 2025;14(8):1185.
source.provenance_note: Compiled manually from the published article. No model-generated values are treated as source evidence.

design.blocking: Randomized complete block design conducted separately in each of three durian orchards; four treatments; three replicates per treatment; 12 durian trees per treatment.
design.notes: The paper states the randomized complete block design and replication structure but does not explicitly identify the physical randomization unit.

population.notes: Selected orchards were approximately 0.4-0.5 ha with 110-140 trees. Trees used for the experiment had similar trunk and stem diameters. Pest and weed control were applied uniformly.

provenance.locator: Section 4.1 Study Location, Soil, Plants, and Climate

interventions.name: Common background NPK fertilization
interventions.dose_text: 0.45 kg N, 0.45 kg P, and 0.45 kg K per tree
interventions.timing_text: 30% at 25 days after fruit set; 40% at 50 days after fruit set; 30% at 35 days before fruit harvest
interventions.notes: Applied uniformly to all treatment arms; therefore it is background management rather than the experimental contrast.

interventions.name: Organic manure
interventions.product_name: Commercial organic fertilizer from PPE Co., Ltd.
interventions.composition_text: Sugarcane filter cake was the primary feedstock. The paper reports total C 15.4%, porosity 76.2%, exchangeable K 15.0 cmolc kg^-1, exchangeable Ca 61.6 cmolc kg^-1, and available P 3.6 g kg^-1, with nutrient composition attributed to a previous study.
interventions.frequency_text: One application per season as described
interventions.notes: Commercial organic manure produced in Can Tho City, Vietnam.

interventions.name: Foliar fertilization
interventions.composition_text: Authors report, according to the producer, 4% K2O and 4.3% Ca.
interventions.notes: The article describes timing and product composition but does not state the applied spray dose/concentration in Sections 4.2-4.3.

arms.label: Control
arms.notes: Control means unamended with OM or FF; it still received the common NPK program.

outcomes.sampling_rule: Soil at 0-20 cm sampled around the canopy at three points 1 m from the trunk and mixed into one sample; 72 samples in total (4 treatments x 3 replicates x 3 sites x 2 seasons).

flags.detail: The article identifies TANO 708, its reported K2O/Ca composition, and the three application times, but the applied spray dose or concentration is not stated in Sections 4.2-4.3.
Table 2 reports the D1, 2022-2023, OM leaf-K cell as '13.9 b ± 035'. The decimal point in the reported SD is ambiguous, so dispersion_value is left unresolved rather than silently corrected.
Table 4 reports the D2, 2023-2024 Control b* value as 37.3 c ± 11.8. The SD is unusually large relative to neighboring cells. It is preserved exactly as published and not corrected.

The article reports a randomized complete block design with three replicates and 12 trees per treatment, but does not explicitly identify the physical randomization unit. The compiler therefore does not infer tree, plot, or replicate as the randomization unit. Every derived treatment-minus-control difference is therefore a descriptive difference of published arm means; the unit of inference and the independence of replicates are unknown.

Fruit-quality outcomes (PD rate, peel/seed/aril proportions, aril b* and TSS) were measured on three randomly selected fruits per replicate, restricted to 2.2-2.8 kg and no physical pest damage. Because this selection happens after treatment, these outcomes describe sound fruit in that weight range and are narrower than orchard-wide fruit-level outcomes. Fruit yield (all fruit weighed), soil and leaf outcomes are not subject to this rule.

flags.detail: Treating the n = 72 stated in the Table 5 caption as 72 independent pairs, a two-sided Pearson test implies p < 0.05 for |r| >= 0.232 and p < 0.01 for |r| >= 0.302. Reading '*' as 0.01 <= p < 0.05, '**' as p < 0.01 and no mark as p >= 0.05, 17 of 36 printed annotations disagree: 7 correlations carry no star although |r| >= 0.232 (a disagreement under any reading of the stars) and 10 carry a single star although |r| >= 0.302. Under an inclusive reading of '*' (p < 0.05 even when p is smaller) only the 7 unmarked cells disagree. The printed r values and stars are preserved unchanged. This does not show that the authors' tests were wrong: the pooled observations are probably not 72 independent pairs, and the number of observations behind each leaf and fruit variable is not stated. The related records are the correlations whose printed annotation disagrees with the independent-pairs check.

Table 5 correlations pool observations across treatments, sites and seasons (n = 72 is the stated total; the soil samples are 4 treatments x 3 replicates x 3 sites x 2 seasons). They are descriptive associations of pooled values: treatment arms, orchards and seasons are mixed, observations from the same orchard, season or replicate are probably not independent, and soil and leaf values were measured after treatment. They are not intervention effects and not evidence that changing one soil or leaf variable would change the PD rate. The paper does not state the unit behind each observation for leaf and fruit variables.

Section 4.6 states that Duncan's post hoc test (p < 0.05) was used to identify differences among treatments. The table footnotes say 'Different letters indicate significance at p < 0.05 (*), p < 0.01 (**), and p < 0.001 (***)' (Table 1; the other tables list the levels they use), which ties letters to the asterisk levels printed in each table's p-value row without naming the omnibus test behind that row. The compiled families keep the printed letters and the printed marker separately, attribute the letters to the Duncan procedure at alpha 0.05 as stated in Section 4.6, and do not infer the omnibus test.
